drivers.reason: 51 leads directly to Pune communities in62. The Vaswani pair and the Sita Mai / Ganore group remain intact;61 keeps Brahma Kumaris and its separate Kolhapur cohorts.
Begin with Kerala52, follow the Tamil and Vaishnava aisle to57, then turn toward Karnataka68 and return through Andhra and the southern continuation to51.
Uniform18 remains with the Sikh display; the distinct Haridwar spade moves from64 to70 with northern context.17 retains the other large Sikh relic allowance.
Gajanan, Bhaskar and Vasudev move together to3. Datta affiliation is traditional devotional recognition, not a newly asserted direct guru–disciple relationship.

drivers.connection: Haidakhan family restores the upper display74
drivers.reason: The existing three-personFAM-018 display family moves intact one case along the northern row.22 retains Bhoomanand and northern companions;74 keeps identity-review holdings separately below.
Neem Karoli joins Samarth Ramdas as a thematic West–North–Vraj bridge. Sevakdas moves to the Pune display62 to retain the space comparison.

Pushkar39/40 and Girnar58–60 stay coherent; Prayagraj27 is distinct. Case29 includes a labelled Chitrakoot/Rama continuation beside Tulsidas36 while keeping Kabir and Kashi personal groups intact. No new historical relationships are asserted.

tradeoffs: Published for curator review as a proposed arrangement. Recorded current locations and physical move confirmations are preserved.
The uniform relocation is approved as a proposal. Physical execution is not confirmed; other exploratory allocations remain for review.
17 and 70 are provisional Sikh mounting allowances, not confirmed free capacity.
The Buddhist display shares 25 with separately labelled eastern cohorts; this is not a new tradition or personal relationship.
The South uses 63 and 65–68 around protected 64/69; those fixed objects interrupt the visual southern run until housing is resolved.
Samarth Ramdas 80 and the Ramanandi story are a cross-aisle thematic connection, not a shared guru lineage.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Start in Kerala
visitorStoryRoute.people: Shivaprabhakara and Kerala families
visitorStoryRoute.story: Begin on the southern side at 52. Follow the same aisle through Tamil and Sri Vaishnava settings toward the highlight case 57.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Tamil Shaiva settings
visitorStoryRoute.people: Pamban Swamigal and Tamil companion groups
visitorStoryRoute.story: Continue along the aisle. Keep Pamban’s local story legible alongside the other Tamil devotional settings.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Chennai and Puducherry
visitorStoryRoute.people: Chennai groups · Naagalinga Swami Sidhar
visitorStoryRoute.story: Naagalinga joins 54 from 63, beside the Tamil Siddha settings. Arrange the smaller local cohorts around the reviewed families.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Sri Vaishnava settings
visitorStoryRoute.people: Srirangam Jeeyars · Hatiram / Hathiram identity-held grouping
visitorStoryRoute.story: Srirangam temple and teaching groups form a distinct cluster. Keep the Tirupati story separate; preserve the existing Hatiram identity question.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Southern highlights
visitorStoryRoute.people: Ramanujacharya · Ramana Maharshi · Bhagavan Nityananda
visitorStoryRoute.story: Three distinct spiritual settings share the prime endcap. Nityananda’s four-person family stays together; his Kerala work opens a connection back toward Ganeshpuri in the West.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Turn toward Karnataka
visitorStoryRoute.people: Hubli–Mugalkhod families
visitorStoryRoute.story: From 57, turn toward 68 and begin the return along the southern row.17 retains the other large Sikh relic mounting provision; check that fit before the southern reuse.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Andhra: Guntur and Ram Nam
visitorStoryRoute.people: Ragam Rama Pitchaiah Garu · reviewed Andhra avadhuta families
visitorStoryRoute.story: Continue from 68 to 67 and 66. Keep the Ram Nam group and each immediate guru family together within the Guntur / Andhra setting.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Kadapa and Andhra families
visitorStoryRoute.people: Veerabrahmendra · Siddhaiah
visitorStoryRoute.story: The teacher and disciple provide the Andhra anchor, with their close family kept together.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Hyderabad and southern holdings
visitorStoryRoute.people: Nampally Baba · Mallesh Baba · separate southern entries
visitorStoryRoute.story: Finish the return row at 63. The Hyderabad-labelled pair and the other entries retain their own identities and locality qualifications; Naagalinga has moved to 54.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Puducherry–Pune bridge
visitorStoryRoute.people: The Mother · Dilip Kumar Roy · Indira Devi
visitorStoryRoute.story: 51 turns the southern route toward the West. Keep this immediate group together, then continue directly to the Pune display in neighbouring 62.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Pune communities
visitorStoryRoute.people: T.L. Vaswani and J.P. Vaswani · Sita Mai and Ganore Baba
visitorStoryRoute.story: The former 46 cohort and the intact Bhukum pair from 47 join 62. Keep each family distinct inside the Pune-facing display beside 51.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Mount Abu and Kolhapur contexts
visitorStoryRoute.people: Brahma Kumaris · distinct Kolhapur companion cohorts
visitorStoryRoute.story: The former 62 cohort moves intact to 61. Read the Brahma Kumaris and the Kolhapur groups as separate stories within this case.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Girnar and Rajasthan
visitorStoryRoute.people: Girnar communities · Dadu Dayal
visitorStoryRoute.story: Follow the western face toward the Rajasthan end. The Girnar settings and Dadu’s tradition keep their separate local and devotional identities.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Girnar–Nath continuation
visitorStoryRoute.people: Girnar families · Gorakhnath / Nath context
visitorStoryRoute.story: Cross to 46 with the former 61 group intact. Its Girnar and Nath contexts connect onward into the existing western island.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Western companion families
visitorStoryRoute.people: Pundalik and Anashuya groups · other Maharashtra companions
visitorStoryRoute.story: Gajanan’s Shegaon family now sits together in the Datta highlight 3. Sita Mai and Ganore Baba are with the Pune display 62; the remaining companion cohorts retain their own groups here.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Nath and western communities
visitorStoryRoute.people: Nath traditions · Jalaram · other western city groups
visitorStoryRoute.story: Continue along the western island, then turn through 39 and 40 toward the Nivrittinath–Dnyaneshwar hinge.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Varkari devotion
visitorStoryRoute.people: Dnyaneshwar · Eknath · Savata Mali · Namdev and Janabai · Tukaram
visitorStoryRoute.story: Follow the Varkari run toward the prominent Tukaram display 45. Preserve close companions without treating the whole movement as one guru succession.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Shirdi, Sakori and Meher Baba
visitorStoryRoute.people: Shirdi Sai Baba · Upasani and Godavari · Meher Baba’s formation circle
visitorStoryRoute.story: Personal connections hold this display together across several western centres. Keep each close pair visible within the larger circle.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Datta families
visitorStoryRoute.people: Dattatreya · Narasimha Saraswati · Akkalkot family · Gajanan, Bhaskar and Vasudev
visitorStoryRoute.story: Gajanan’s existing three-person Shegaon group joins 3. The broader grouping reflects attested Datta devotional affiliation; it adds no direct Akkalkot guru–disciple claim. Vasudev’s footprint remains unknown.

visitorStoryRoute.title: BAPS succession
visitorStoryRoute.people: The BAPS guru family
visitorStoryRoute.story: One case presents the immediate succession together, with room to read its relationships.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Punjab and the Sikh gurus
visitorStoryRoute.people: Guru Nanak and Sri Chand · Sikh guru families · uniform
visitorStoryRoute.story: Follow the Sikh and Udasi families along the wall to the uniform in 18.17 retains the other large Sikh relic mounting provision. The separate Haridwar spade is next in 70.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Haridwar’s full-height relic
visitorStoryRoute.people: Hanuman Das of Haridwar
visitorStoryRoute.story: The spade moves from its former proposed 64 position to 70, beside the northern wall and the Sikh display. It retains northern context and separate full-height housing; the uniform remains 18.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Badrinath
visitorStoryRoute.people: Badrinarayana · Badrinath companion groups
visitorStoryRoute.story: A Himalayan pilgrimage setting gathers the Badrinath-related displays.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Uttarkashi and Rishikesh
visitorStoryRoute.people: Tapovan · Chinmayananda
visitorStoryRoute.story: Keep the teacher and disciple together. Nearby smaller displays gather around their meaningful Himalayan cities.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Rishikesh teaching family
visitorStoryRoute.people: Sivananda · Chidananda · Vishnudevananda
visitorStoryRoute.story: The immediate teaching family remains together across the places where its work spread.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Northern review holdings
visitorStoryRoute.people: Identity under review
visitorStoryRoute.story: These labelled holdings retain their identity questions while the curator reviews them.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Kumaon
visitorStoryRoute.people: Haidakhan Babaji · Neem Karoli Baba
visitorStoryRoute.story: The Kumaon setting leads toward Neem Karoli’s North–Vraj connection. The Nainital marker is a regional reference, not an exact ashram location.

visitorStoryRoute.title: The Kriya tree
visitorStoryRoute.people: Babaji · Lahiri · Sri Yukteswar · Yogananda · related disciples
visitorStoryRoute.story: Keep the clear Kriya tree together in 5. Its Varanasi and Bengal lives make it a natural bridge between North and East.
visitorStoryRoute.transition: Mahendranath Gupta supplies the personal connection into the next display.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Ramakrishna’s family
visitorStoryRoute.people: Ramakrishna · Vivekananda · Mahendranath Gupta · Lakshmi Mani
visitorStoryRoute.story: The Dakshineswar/Kolkata setting anchors this family. Place Mahendranath Gupta toward Kriya to make his encounter with Yogananda easy to see.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Anandamayi Ma
visitorStoryRoute.people: Anandamayi Ma and her immediate family
visitorStoryRoute.story: Keep the mobile family together across Bengal and Kankhal. These two map markers orient the wider story; they are not a complete life route.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Shakta and Jaiguru settings
visitorStoryRoute.people: Bamakhepa · Omkarnath · Parankush and Jaiguru
visitorStoryRoute.story: Distinct local settings sit beside intact teaching families. Jaiguru connects Bengal and Puri without being split between them.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Eastern and Buddhist settings
visitorStoryRoute.people: Assam and Bengal groups · distinct Buddhist display
visitorStoryRoute.story: Give Assam, Bengal and the Buddhist display their own identities inside this shared allocation.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Puri and Odisha
visitorStoryRoute.people: Jagannath · Gosaiji · Yogmaya · Kuladananda
visitorStoryRoute.story: Puri leads into Gosaiji’s immediate family at the Vraj-facing endcap. Keep Cuttack and Nemalo-related smaller cohorts legible as their own local settings.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Gaudiya teaching families
visitorStoryRoute.people: Bhaktisiddhanta · Prabhupada · Jagadbandhu · Tinkodi–Murari · Radharaman Charan Das
visitorStoryRoute.story: The Gaudiya story crosses Bengal, Puri and Vraj. Keep each immediate branch together rather than treating the full tradition as a single household.

visitorStoryRoute.title: The Mirabai hinge
visitorStoryRoute.people: Mirabai · Chaitanya and early Gaudiyas · Ravidas · Vraj Ramanandis
visitorStoryRoute.story: Independently prominent saints carry the bridge across neighbouring displays. Their distinct settings remain visible as the story turns toward Ram devotion.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Ram devotion and Kashi
visitorStoryRoute.people: Tulsidas and Hanuman · Kabir · Trailanga and Shankari
visitorStoryRoute.story: Rama devotion leads into Kashi. Keep the close pairs together; preserve the different meanings of traditional relationships and personal encounters.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Ram devotion from the West
visitorStoryRoute.people: Samarth Ramdas
visitorStoryRoute.story: The western Ram-bhakti story meets the Ramanandi side of the hinge through shared devotion, while retaining its own lineage.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Vraj’s local traditions
visitorStoryRoute.people: Banke Bihari · Radha Raman · Surdas and Pushtimarg · modern Vraj groups
visitorStoryRoute.story: Adjacent deity displays begin a local Vraj story. Continue through the different traditions and keep Devraha–Devra Hansa and other close families together.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Bhakti Marga and global contexts
visitorStoryRoute.people: Bhakti Marga families and global connections
visitorStoryRoute.story: These displays extend the museum’s Indian stories into the wider world.

visitorStoryRoute.title: Walking-stick displays
visitorStoryRoute.people: Fixed walking-stick housing
visitorStoryRoute.story: Walking sticks remain in their dedicated vitrines, with their saint connections retained.

1.reason: The Datta family has a compact prime anchor.

2.reason: The compact Kriya family uses 2 → 78 → 36 → 29, with the other northern families continuing up the same face. Exact primary positions remain pending.

3.people: Shirdi Sai Baba and Meher Baba’s formation circle
3.reason: The Sai families continue through the central island.

4.reason: Continue toward 6–7 on the right wall.

5.reason: Keep the devotional bridge together in 5 → 74 → 22. Exact primary positions remain pending.

45.reason: Swaminarayan / BAPS follows 45 → 44 → 43; Varkari follows 42 → 41 → 40 → 39 on the same face.

57.reason: The eastern family sequence now follows 57 → 56 → 55 → 54 → 53 → 52 → 51 along the opposite face of the entrance island.

drivers.reason: The three southern island cases 19 / 20 / 72 now directly face southern wall cases 18 / 17 / 16. The northern row no longer sits between them.

drivers.connection: Other western families join the entrance-room West
drivers.reason: The entire five-case family envelope moves from 27 / 28 / 76 / 29 / 36 to 62 → 61 → 60 → 59 → 58. Gujarat, Maharashtra, Datta and Brahma Kumaris remain together in their existing immediate families.
The Sai / Meher Baba island retains the same four cases, preserving the flow from the entrance-room western neighbourhood and the immediate Sai families.
The eastern families follow the lower face and end caps: 57 → 56 → 55 → 54 → 53 → 52 → 51. Buddhist context is nearby at 63, across the short aisle; it keeps a separate identity.
Varkari retains 39 → 40 → 41 → 42, with Dnyaneshwar toward the shared end at 39 / 50. Nath retains 50 → 49 → 48 → 47 → 46. Nivrittinath is historical context; no matching relic record was identified.
The traditional devotional bridge moves as one three-case group. Preserve the traditional teacher association and shared Ramanandi-context labels.

drivers.connection: Bhakti Marga / global context moves together
drivers.reason: The two-case context group moves from 63 / 64 to the freed cave-end cap and adjoining case, 37 / 26. This provides the additional entrance-room case needed to retain all eight eastern cases and all five other-western cases.

largeObjects.fallback: If the proposed uniform case lacks clearance, retain the large objects in 23 until a suitable neighbouring Sikh case is confirmed.
largeObjects.note: Uniform → 69 beside Sikh 65–68, subject to clearance. Plow / source-described spade stays in 23. Sticks stay in 30–31.

tradeoffs: Five western cases replace four flexible cases in the entrance room. Moving Buddhist context to 63 and the two-case Bhakti Marga / global group to 37 / 26 preserves every regional case allowance and all six flexible cases.
Gaudiya families remain on one right-island face, while the Mirabai–Ravidas–Kabir group takes the left prime end. Their immediate family envelopes stay intact.
Gaudiya–Puri, Kriya–Ramakrishna, western–southern Datta and Vaswani–Ramana remain interpretive bridges across neighbourhoods.
Case dimensions, mounting clearance and irregular relic fit remain on-site checks. Exact primary placements are deferred.
